AnalysisOutcome.description: Whether the tested effect produced any finding at the threshold the source applied. Closed: the two are the only answers, and a source that does not say takes `not_reported` rather than a third value.
AnalysisOutcome.title: AnalysisOutcome

AnalysisType.description: The method that produced the statistical map, independent of what was tested about it. A between-group comparison of connectivity, decoding accuracy, or component loadings keeps the method here and records the comparison in Effect. Bound only by ConjunctionComponent.analysis_type; an Analysis states its method by which AnalysisDetails subclass it fills. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
AnalysisType.title: AnalysisType

AnalysisVerdict.description:
pondie's verdict on one analysis of the parse a revision revises, reached while extracting the whole record. The verdict overrides the original's proposal, grouping and role alike.
What a verdict does to what is stored against the analysis -- claims, their evidence, and users' votes on them:
- accept, relabel: nothing moves. The key is unchanged, so everything stored against
  it applies to the revision as it stands.
- split: everything is copied to each analysis in `replaced_by`. - merge: everything stored against each merged analysis is copied to the one
  analysis they merge into. Two copies of the same field with the same value become
  one claim; with different values they stay competing claims, resolved like any
  other.
- omit: nothing is copied. - add: nothing to copy; the analysis is new.
Every copy records the key and parse it was copied from, so a reviewer can tell a copied claim from one made against the revision. The revised parse and everything stored against it are kept, unchanged, as history: superseded rather than deleted, and left out of projections and studysets.

evidence.description: The sentences of the paper the verdict rests on.

key.description: The revised parse's analysis key; for `add`, the new analysis's key in this revision.

replaced_by.description: The keys in this revision that take the analysis's place: itself for accept and relabel, the replacements for split and merge, none for omit.

role.description: For relabel, the role the points have instead.

AnalysisVerdict.title: AnalysisVerdict

CoordinateParse.description:
Every coordinate a paper reports, grouped into analyses. An original parse is written by the ingestion workflow; a revision is written by pondie when its audit disagrees with the original.
A parse is never edited after it is written. A reader that disagrees with it writes a revision instead, and the revision is a complete parse on its own: neurostore can store it as a new version of the paper's analyses without consulting the parse it revises.
Analyses that pondie accepts or relabels keep their keys, because their name, space and points are unchanged, so claims made against them carry over to the revision untouched. Only a split, a merge or an omission changes which keys exist.

analyses.description: May be empty: the parse ran and found no analysis. A paper the parse never ran on has no CoordinateParse at all, so the two are never confused, and `tables` says what reading each table found.

header.description: `inputs` names the parsed paper by `text_sha256`, and for a revision also the parse it revises by `parse_id`.

omitted_analyses.description: Text or figure analyses the producer read and left out of `analyses`, each with the reason. A table's omissions are in `tables`. Absent when nothing was left out.

parse_id.description: This parse's identity, the fingerprint every later artifact cites. Unique per paper; a sha256 of the canonical JSON of `analyses` is recommended, so two producers that reach the same analyses reach the same id.

revision_of.description: The `parse_id` of the parse this one revises. Absent on an original parse, which is how a reader tells the two apart.

tables.description: One entry per table of the parsed paper: what reading it for coordinates found, or why it was not read. A table with no entry was not considered.

text_sha256.description: The parsed paper's fingerprint. Every point's cells and spans address it.

text_sweep.description: How much of the text was searched for coordinates outside tables. Absent when the text was not searched.

verdicts.description: On a revision only: one verdict for every analysis of the revised parse, so nothing in it is silently dropped, and an `add` verdict for every analysis the revision introduces that the revised parse lacked. An original parse has none.

CoordinateParse.title: CoordinateParse

CoordinateRole.description: What a set of reported coordinates is, by what it is to the study and not by where the paper prints it. A coordinate that appears in a figure takes the role of what it is: peaks the study found are results even when a figure shows them. The role is judged for the coordinate-based meta-analysis these coordinates feed. When a set could be a `result` or another role, it is a `result`: a result missed costs the meta-analysis more than a non-result kept. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording when nothing here fits.
CoordinateRole.title: CoordinateRole

Correction.description: One notice attached to a paper.
Correction.title: Correction

CorrectionKind.description: A notice attached to a paper by its publisher or indexer.
CorrectionKind.title: CorrectionKind

CorrectionMethod.description: How a p value or threshold was corrected for multiple comparisons.
CorrectionMethod.title: CorrectionMethod

DecompositionMethod.description: The algorithm that produced the components or latent variables, which decides what their values and signs mean. Independent of `second_block`, since one block structure is reachable by several algorithms: a brain-behaviour covariance can be decomposed by PLS or by CCA. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
DecompositionMethod.title: DecompositionMethod

Direction.description:
How a term entered or came out of an analysis, using one vocabulary for every term type. Both a categorical level on the plus side of a comparison and a continuous term with a positive coefficient are `positive`. The referenced term's `type` distinguishes them. For a cell over a **product** term, this field gives the interaction coefficient's sign, not either component's slope.
It is a sign, not a magnitude: numeric contrast weights are never recorded, and a contrast whose magnitudes matter keeps them in `Analysis.definition`. There is no value for a zero weight either -- a level the contrast did not weight has no `Cell` at all.
Only `positive` and `negative` are directional. A cell can record no sign three ways -- `undirected`, `held`, or `extraction_status: not_reported` -- and choosing between them is the decision rule in extraction-readme.md §2.
Direction.title: Direction

DocumentSource.description: Where the parsed text came from. Open vocabulary: a new source is added here when it is added to the download order, not discovered by a consumer.
DocumentSource.title: DocumentSource

EdgeDirectionality.description:
Whether a connectivity edge is genuinely directed. Only directed models such as DCM and Granger causality qualify; a seed-to-voxel PPI or correlation is undirected, and its sign travels with the edge rather than implying a direction.
The one vocabulary nothing reads off the page: `ConnectivityEdge.directionality` is derived from `ConnectivityDetails.connectivity_method`, since the method decides it and no wording can override it.
EdgeDirectionality.title: EdgeDirectionality

EffectKind.description:
What kind of test an effect's cells describe. The range of `Effect.kind`, and also the output of deriving the same thing from the cells -- the two are compared, and a disagreement is a record contradicting itself.
This once had no slot at all, on the reasoning that the kind follows entirely from the cells and storing it would put one fact in two places. It does put it in two places, and that turned out to be the reason to store it: a cell pattern that derives nothing, or derives something other than what the analysis is, was invisible while the record stated the shape only once. There is no free-text branch: a cell pattern yields one of these labels or none, and a pattern yielding none is a record whose cells do not describe a test. The derivation is stated once, in extraction-readme.md §3.
EffectKind.title: EffectKind

EffectPath.description:
The path through a mediation model represented by an effect's map. Without it, an indirect-effect map is structurally identical to a plain regression on the same predictor, and a synthesis would pool the two.
No `not_applicable` value is needed: an effect outside a mediated path has no `Mediation` object or slot to fill.
EffectPath.title: EffectPath

FunctionalForm.description: Shape of a term's relationship to the measure. A squared term with a negative coefficient is an inverted-U relationship, not a negative association, so non-linear and transformed terms must not be reported as linear. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
FunctionalForm.title: FunctionalForm

InferenceTarget.description: What the connectivity analysis drew inference about. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
InferenceTarget.title: InferenceTarget

InputRef.description: One artifact another was made from.

artifact_kind.description: A parse ArtifactKind, or the name of another artifact kind such as an extraction record or a downloaded file.

fingerprint.description: The input's identity: `text_sha256` for a parsed paper, `parse_id` for a coordinate parse, a sha256 otherwise.

InputRef.title: InputRef

MapQuantity.description: What the values of a component or latent-variable map represent. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
MapQuantity.title: MapQuantity

MeasureFamily.description: Broad imaging or signal family, for coarse filtering. A BOLD-derived connectivity or decoding result stays functional_bold: derived measures take the family of the underlying signal. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
MeasureFamily.title: MeasureFamily

MeasureType.description: Normalized scientific quantity of the map, for cross-study queries. Activation and deactivation are directions rather than measure types; both are bold_response and the directional roles carry the direction. Gray-matter density is not collapsed into volume. A paper that does not identify the measure leaves the slot `extraction_status: not_reported`. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.

NotStructurableReason.description: Why a grounded effect has no stable structured decomposition. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
NotStructurableReason.title: NotStructurableReason

NullHypothesis.description: The null hypothesis tested by a conjunction. Only the conjunction null supports the interpretation that every component effect is present, so the hypothesis is recorded separately from the procedure that implemented it.
NullHypothesis.title: NullHypothesis

OmittedAnalysis.description: A text or figure analysis the producer read but did not keep, the text counterpart of a `TableReading` with a reason.

name.description: The analysis's label as the producer read it.

reason.description: Why it was left out, for example that it repeats a kept analysis (the same key) or that its passage is not in the text.

text_spans.description: The sentences it was read from, when it was located.

OmittedAnalysis.title: OmittedAnalysis

ParsedAnalysis.description:
The points a paper reports together for one tested effect, or for one non-result purpose such as the regions of interest an analysis used.
In an original parse, the grouping is the ingestion workflow's proposal, made from a table and its caption. pondie confirms or overrides it with the whole paper in view. The role is required and is set in the ingestion workflow by the `roles` classifier stage, after the analyses are identified. It is also the ingestion workflow's proposal: pondie's accept confirms it, and a relabel overrides it with a reviewed correction that wins.

cells.description: For a table analysis, every cell it was read from: each point's row and column group, and the rows that name the contrast without coordinates. Required for `origin: table`; every point's row and column group is among them.

coordinate_space.description: The space of the analysis's points; absent when the paper states none. A point states its own only when it differs.

derived_from.description: On a revision, the keys of the revised parse's analyses this one was made from by a split or a merge. Absent on an analysis carried over unchanged.

from_prior_study.description: The coordinates come from another publication rather than from this study: a peak quoted for comparison (always true for `role: reference`), another study's peak taken as this study's ROI or seed, or a peak from the authors' own earlier publication given with its statistics, which is `role: result` with this flag true so that a meta-analysis can avoid counting the earlier study twice. Separate from the role, because a borrowed seed is still the seed this study's analysis used. False when the study defined them itself, including an ROI built from its own earlier result, meaning an earlier analysis in this same paper such as a localizer.

key.description:
The analysis's identity, derived from what was extracted -- its `name`, `coordinate_space` and `points` -- never from where it was read, so the same analysis read from two sources (a table and its HTML copy, a table and the sentence restating it) reaches the same key, and a re-run that extracts the same content reaches it again. A rename or a changed point is a new key. The name is part of the key because differently named analyses can print identical points.
`analysis#<h>`, where `h` is the first 16 hex characters of the sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the compact JSON array `[<name>, <space>, [<point>, ...]]` (no whitespace, non-ASCII characters unescaped). `<name>` is `name` normalized: Unicode NFKC, casefolded, every dash (Unicode Pd and U+2212 minus) as `-`, zero-width characters and all whitespace dropped, so `PO > Sil` and `PO>Sil` are one name. `<space>` is `coordinate_space`, or `""` when absent.
Each `<point>` is `[<x>, <y>, <z>, <space>, [[<kind>, <value>], ...]]`: the coordinates rounded to 0.01 mm and written with two decimals (`"-4.00"`); the point's own `space` when it differs from the analysis's, else `""`; and each of its `values` as its `kind` and its value written to 6 significant digits (`"5.8"`, `"3.2e-12"`). Negative zero is written as zero. Each point's values, and then the points, are sorted by their own compact JSON, in code point order.
An analysis with no points -- a contrast a table lists as "n.s." -- hashes its name and space alone. The two halves of a sign split hold different points under different names, so each has its own key. `study_schema.keys.analysis_key` computes it.
This key is what the extraction record's `Analysis.source_table_analysis` and `CoordinateSet.id` name, and what neurostore stores as `Analysis.source_id`. Two analyses of one parse never share a name, space and points, so never share a key.

name.description: The analysis's label, as printed where the paper prints one.

name_is_printed.description: False when the producer composed the name because the paper printed none, so a reader never mistakes a placeholder for the paper's wording.

points.description: Empty when the paper names the analysis but reports no coordinates for it -- most often because nothing survived the threshold. Whether it found an effect is the extraction record's `Analysis.outcome`; an empty list here only says that no coordinates were printed.

prior_study_evidence.description: The citation or sentence showing the coordinates come from another publication.

role.description:
What the points are for. Only a `result` is an analysis with a statistic in the extraction record; an `anchor` -- a region of interest, a seed, a stimulation target -- becomes a CoordinateSet there, and never enters a studyset as an analysis.
Required. Set in the ingestion workflow by the `roles` classifier stage, after the analyses are identified: a classifier that reads each set and its context, named by `role_source`. It is the ingestion workflow's proposal, which pondie audits: accept confirms it, and relabel overrides it with a reviewed correction that wins. The extractors never propose a role, and nothing supplies a default.
Numbers that are not brain coordinates, such as channel numbers or lattice points, get no role. They are not a coordinate set.

role_source.description: The classifier that set the role, by name and version, such as `set-role-encoder@2026-10-09`.

split.description: Present on both halves of an analysis split by sign, and only there. The split is declared here and nowhere else: a reader never infers it from a name.

statistic.description: The test statistic of this analysis's one test -- t, z, F, chi_square -- whatever the columns call it. One analysis is one test. Every value at a point that describes the same test belongs to that point: the statistic, its p value (uncorrected and corrected), an effect size, the cluster's p. A different test is a different analysis, even on the same rows: an omnibus F and the directional post-hoc t that follows it are two analyses, told apart by `column_group` when one table prints both.

statistic_df.description: Degrees of freedom as printed, such as "1, 38" or "27".

table_id.description: The ParsedTable the points were read from. Present exactly when `origin` is `table`.

text_spans.description: For a text or figure analysis, the sentences or legend it was read from: those holding its coordinates, or the one stating a result that has none.

thresholds.description: The thresholds the analysis's results survived, at every level the paper states: most often a voxel-level height ("p < .001 uncorrected") together with a cluster-level correction ("FWE p < .05"), which one method cannot express. Read from the caption, footer or Methods; each threshold cites where.

ParsedAnalysis.title: ParsedAnalysis

ParsedPaper.description:
One paper as text, tables and bibliographic facts. The same shape for every download source.
The text is the only offset space. Every evidence span an extraction record cites, every table row's position and every text-read point addresses `text_sha256`'s characters, so a span can be checked by slicing the text, and a span made against a different text is detectably wrong.

citations.description: Every in-text citation, where it sits in the text and which reference it points to. The link from a sentence to a work, which the reference list alone cannot give: what resolves the citations a task's description makes (storage `Task.reference_ids`) and traces a task to the paper that introduced it.

is_meta_analysis.description: Whether the paper is itself a meta-analysis or review, decided here once. Every consumer reads this field; none applies its own test.

references.description: The paper's reference list, in order. Usually fetched from an API by the paper's identifiers rather than parsed from the text (`Reference.provider` says which), so it is complete and carries DOIs even when the text's list is badly extracted.

source_reason.description: Why this source's text was chosen over the others downloaded, such as "most tables" or "first in download order". Every stage reads this one text, so the choice is made once and recorded.

supplements.description: Supplementary material the paper links to, and whether it was fetched. A result the text cites to a supplement that was not fetched is reported elsewhere, not missing.

text_path.description: The text file's path, relative to the paper's bundle directory.

text_sha256.description: sha256 of the text file's UTF-8 bytes. This artifact's fingerprint.

ParsedPaper.title: ParsedPaper

ParsedPoint.description: One reported coordinate. `coordinates`, `space` and `values` are NIMADS's point fields with NIMADS's meaning, so the projection to a studyset copies them; everything else is the parse's own.

column_group.description: For a table point, which block of coordinate columns it was read from, numbered from 0 left to right. 0 in a table with one block. Two contrasts printed side by side share rows and differ here.

label.description: The region name printed beside the point.

row.description: For a table point, the TableRow it was read from.

space.description: Only when it differs from the analysis's `coordinate_space`.

text_span.description: For a text point, the characters it was read from.

values.description: The values at the point. They are the only record of its sign (StatisticKind gives the rule): a negative value makes it negative, and a point with only p, F or chi-square values, or none, is unsigned and takes the side of its analysis's `split` half. On the inverse half the directional statistic values are negated so they read positive; p, F and chi-square stay as printed. `split` declares the inverse half, and a consumer records the inverse on the contrast's conditions (negated weights), not per point. There is no point-level deactivation flag, and the parse never writes neurostore's Point.deactivation.

ParsedPoint.title: ParsedPoint

ParsedTable.description: A table of the paper, cell by cell.

coordinate_space_hint.description: The source parser's own guess at the table's space. A hint for the coordinate stages, not an answer: the space a point is stored in is the coordinate parse's.

label.description: The printed label, such as Table 2 or Supplementary Table S4.

raw_path.description: The source's raw table file, relative to the bundle directory.

rows.description: The body rows, in printed order.

table_id.description: The table's key, as the source's parser names it. Stable for the life of the parsed paper and used unchanged by every consumer: the coordinate parse's `table_id`s, the record's Table.id, neurostore's Table.t_id. Never renumbered from the printed label and never sanitized differently on disk.

text_span.description: Where the table's rows are inlined in the text, when the source inlines them.

ParsedTable.title: ParsedTable

PerformanceRelation.description: Direction of a decoding performance metric relative to its reference value.
PerformanceRelation.title: PerformanceRelation

PointValue.description: A value reported at a point. NIMADS's point value.

correction.description: For a p value, the correction it is under; absent for a statistic or effect size.

level.description: Whether the value describes the peak or the cluster the peak belongs to. A cluster-level p printed on the peak's row is the cluster's.

PointValue.title: PointValue

PolaritySemantics.description: Whether the sign of a component map carries meaning. Decomposition methods can return components whose polarity is arbitrary, in which case a negative loading is not a decrease.
PolaritySemantics.title: PolaritySemantics

Prespecification.description: Whether a contrast was planned before the data were seen. A preregistered primary contrast and a post-hoc sweep from the same paper are not equivalent evidence, and a synthesis that cannot tell them apart cannot address selective reporting.
Prespecification.title: Prespecification

Producer.description: The program and stage that wrote an artifact.

model.description: The language model a stage called, if any.

stage.description: The stage within the producer, such as extract, space or audit.

Producer.title: Producer

Reference.description: One entry of a paper's reference list.

id.description: Stable within the paper: the source's own id where it has one (a JATS `ref` id such as `B12`), else `ref<position>`.

label.description: How the text cites it: the number of a numbered style ("12"), or the author-year key of an author-year style ("Stroop 1935").

position.description: 1-based order in the list, which a numbered citation style cites by.

Reference.title: Reference

ReferenceProvider.description: Where a reference-list entry came from.
ReferenceProvider.title: ReferenceProvider

ReportedSpace.description: The coordinate space a point is in, normalized to the values NiMARE transforms between by `study_schema.spaces.normalize_space`. Absent when no space is stated, or when the wording names both MNI and TAL; never defaulted to MNI: a rat study stored as MNI is a wrong coordinate, and a missing one is an honest gap. What the paper printed stays in `space_as_printed`.
ReportedSpace.title: ReportedSpace

ResultKind.description: The kind of analysis a `result` came from, coarse enough to read from a table or a sentence. An analysis the record models in full states its method in `details` and its test in `Effect.kind`; this is the label for a coordinate set either way. Open vocabulary.
ResultKind.title: ResultKind

SecondBlock.description:
What a decomposition crossed the brain block with, one value per block. This decides whether two decompositions answer the same question, so it is the payload's one required vocabulary -- a task PLS and a behavioural PLS are not poolable, and neither is a one-block ICA with either of them.
Multivalued, and `none` is a value rather than an absent field: a one-block decomposition is a positive assertion, not a gap. Name the blocks and not their number -- a design-plus-behaviour PLS is `[design, behavioral]`, and the count follows from the list's length.
Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
SecondBlock.title: SecondBlock

Section.description: A span of the text and what it is.
Section.title: Section

SectionKind.description: What a span of the text is.
SectionKind.title: SectionKind

SignSplit.description:
One half of an analysis the producer split by the sign of its points (see StatisticKind). The original half is the analysis as named and holds the points whose printed values are positive or unsigned. The inverse half is the reversed contrast and holds the points printed negative, whose directional statistic values are negated so they read positive. p, F and chi-square are unsigned and stay as printed, except a value printed negative, which counts as signed and is negated like any other.
`half: inverse` with `original_analysis` (the original's `key`) records the inversion. The inverse half is named by the derived reversed contrast where one can be derived, otherwise "X (inverse)" for the original's name X. Direction lives on the condition weights, not on points: the inverse's weights are the original's, negated. Positive and negative describe statistic values only, never a half: a table of decreases has decreases in its original half.
pondie extracts the original half and derives the inverse half's record from it by flipping the direction of its cells, so the two never disagree and the inverse half costs no extraction. The derived record carries `mirror_of`, which keeps a meta-analysis from counting one contrast twice.
The half lives on the analysis, not its points: an unsigned point (only p, F or chi-square values, or none) in a split analysis is on that analysis's side.

original_analysis.description: On the inverse half, the `key` of the original analysis (the other half of this split) in the same parse. Absent on the original half, and on an inverse half whose original is not in the parse.

SignSplit.title: SignSplit

SpaceBasis.description: Where a space was read from, most specific first.
SpaceBasis.title: SpaceBasis

SpatialScope.description: Spatial domain of the analysis, and a meta-analysis inclusion criterion. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
SpatialScope.title: SpatialScope

SpatialUnit.description: The element an analysis was carried out over: the surface-versus-volume distinction as well as the univariate-versus-parcellated one. Gives the element, where SpatialScope gives the extent. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
SpatialUnit.title: SpatialUnit

SplitHalf.description: Which half of a sign split an analysis is.
SplitHalf.title: SplitHalf

SplitRule.description: The deterministic rule that split an analysis.
SplitRule.title: SplitRule

StatisticFamily.description: Test statistic family for the tested effect, independent of the thresholding procedure recorded in InferenceSettings. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
StatisticFamily.title: StatisticFamily

StatisticKind.description:
The kind of a value reported at a point. One vocabulary for the parse, the extraction record's `Statistic.family`, and neurostore's `PointValue.kind`. The ingestion workflow's letters map one to one: T, Z, F, D, G, R, B, P.
Which side of a sign split a point is on follows from its values:
- A negative value is always on the inverse side, whatever its kind. A negative p, F
  or chi-square means the column is signed or mislabelled.
- Only p, F and chi-square are non-directional. Every other kind is directional,
  `other` included.
- A missing or unknown kind splits by the value's sign, like a directional kind. - A point whose values are all p, F or chi-square, or that has none, is unsigned.
The parse stores no sign of its own; readers derive it from `values` with `study_schema.statistics`.
StatisticKind.title: StatisticKind

path.description: Where the fetched file is, relative to the bundle directory.

TablePurpose.description: What a table is for. A coordinate table is not an analysis merely by having coordinates in it: a study's ROI definitions, its atlas parcels, its connectivity seeds and the peaks of its independent components are all locations rather than findings, and `reported_effect` is what says the rows ARE a finding. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording when nothing here fits.

reason.description: For a table not read, why; for an excluded one, who excluded it.

Threshold.description: One threshold an analysis's results survived. Maps onto the storage schema's InferenceSettings: a `height` threshold is height_threshold_value and _type, a `cluster_extent` is cluster_extent_threshold, a `cluster_level` is clusterwise_threshold_value, `tfce` sets tfce_used; `correction` is multiple_comparison_method at that level.

value.description: Absent when the paper names the correction but not the number.

VariationLevel.description:
The level at which a term varies -- whether it moves within a participant or only across the sample. A property of **any** term, categorical or continuous: a repeated-measures factor and a trial-wise modulator are both within-subject, and a diagnosis factor and an age covariate are both between-subject.
For a continuous term it is what separates a parametric modulation from a cross-subject regression, and the derived kind of an effect testing it reads this. For a categorical factor it feeds no derivation; it is the factor's scope, and two studies that crossed a factor within participants and between them did not estimate the same thing. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
VariationLevel.title: VariationLevel

description:
Every coordinate a paper reports, grouped into analyses. An original parse is written by the ingestion workflow; a revision is written by pondie when its audit disagrees with the original.
A parse is never edited after it is written. A reader that disagrees with it writes a revision instead, and the revision is a complete parse on its own: neurostore can store it as a new version of the paper's analyses without consulting the parse it revises.
Analyses that pondie accepts or relabels keep their keys, because their name, space and points are unchanged, so claims made against them carry over to the revision untouched. Only a split, a merge or an omission changes which keys exist.

analyses.description: May be empty: the parse ran and found no analysis. A paper the parse never ran on has no CoordinateParse at all, so the two are never confused, and `tables` says what reading each table found.

header.description: `inputs` names the parsed paper by `text_sha256`, and for a revision also the parse it revises by `parse_id`.

omitted_analyses.description: Text or figure analyses the producer read and left out of `analyses`, each with the reason. A table's omissions are in `tables`. Absent when nothing was left out.

parse_id.description: This parse's identity, the fingerprint every later artifact cites. Unique per paper; a sha256 of the canonical JSON of `analyses` is recommended, so two producers that reach the same analyses reach the same id.

revision_of.description: The `parse_id` of the parse this one revises. Absent on an original parse, which is how a reader tells the two apart.

tables.description: One entry per table of the parsed paper: what reading it for coordinates found, or why it was not read. A table with no entry was not considered.

text_sha256.description: The parsed paper's fingerprint. Every point's cells and spans address it.

text_sweep.description: How much of the text was searched for coordinates outside tables. Absent when the text was not searched.

verdicts.description: On a revision only: one verdict for every analysis of the revised parse, so nothing in it is silently dropped, and an `add` verdict for every analysis the revision introduces that the revised parse lacked. An original parse has none.
